National Assembly
Complete Record of Proceedings
24 Bhadra 2083
Wednesday
Meeting No. - 44
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 13:28 hours under the chairmanship of the Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the proceedings of today's (13:28 hrs) meeting of the National Assembly are now in session. Honourable members, names have been received to speak during the Zero Hour. I will now provide time for the Honourable members to speak. First, Honourable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya.
Rokaya Rokaya (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, it has been confirmed that more than 2358 people died in the flood in the Bhote Koshi River on the 10th of Bhadra, while more than approximately 5300 have gone missing. I express my heartfelt condolences to those who lost their lives and deep sympathy to their families. Honourable Chairperson, approximately 66 districts of the country have been affected by the flood, and the most affected are the elderly, pregnant women, new mothers, and children. According to the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), it is estimated that there are about 4430 pregnant women in 14 local levels affected by the flood in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, and it is estimated that about 492 babies may be born in one month and about 74 women may require emergency delivery services. Health has not been a priority since the Bhote Koshi flood disaster. I would like to draw the attention of the Nepal government through the Honourable Chairperson to these matters. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Ghanshyam Rizal.
Honourable Mr. Ghanshyam Rizal (Nepali Communist Party): Honourable Chairperson, our country is facing unimaginable loss due to the devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi River on 10th Bhadra, 2083. I offer my heartfelt condolences to all those who lost their lives in this tragic hour and express deep sympathy to their families. I also wish a speedy recovery to all those undergoing treatment. Chairperson, although the initial response of the government during the disaster gave hope, the delay in rescue, relief, and rehabilitation due to a lack of necessary coordination with the press and local governments in the subsequent days of the disaster is regrettable. The delay in rescue has increased the despair and anger among the public, especially for citizens trapped and missing in the landslide. I wish to draw the government's attention to this. Chairperson, it is said that glacial lakes, including Tsho Rolpa in Dolakha, are at risk of bursting due to global warming. I wish to draw the government's attention to conducting immediate technical assessments, installing an early warning system, and making necessary preparations to minimize damage if a disaster occurs. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.
Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, it has been more than 2 weeks since the landslide in Krishnabhir, and the Prithvi Highway, known as the lifeline of the capital, has not yet fully come into operation. Citizens are stranded on the road during the time of disaster and festivals. Citizens are forced to travel via the alternative route through Hetauda and by air. Honourable Chairperson, the cracks seen in Krishnabhir should not be taken lightly; a team of experts should be sent to study it and find solutions for long-term problems such as bridges, alternative roads, and retaining walls. I want to ask if the pride and arrogance of the minister who said the contractor's leg was broken have been broken, who could not even build 2000 meters of dirt road in 2 weeks, and if this is the 'Balen government'? Similarly, while the country is struggling with disaster, airfare has increased from 2000 to 4000 rupees. I wish to draw the serious attention of the Honourable Minister of Tourism to this matter. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Puja Chaudhary.
Honourable Ms. Puja Chaudhary (Janata Samajwadi Party, Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, the citizens of Rasuwa who have lost their families, relatives, homes, and property due to natural disasters are being subjected to insults and derogatory comments on social media, and instead of receiving support, they are blamed and insulted. They receive a shower of abuses on social media when they should be receiving support. It is necessary to immediately stop such activities that hurt the dignity of the victims and spread hatred during such difficult times. Since our Law Minister is also a woman, I hope she understands the suffering of women and, through the Honourable Chairperson, I urge that individuals who spread such anarchy on social media and make comments that cause further pain to the victims be brought under legal process. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Rukmini Koirala.
Honourable Ms. Rukmini Koirala (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honourable Chairperson, today the entire country is in mourning due to a great disaster. At a time when development should be making leaps, we are in a situation where we have to collect decomposed bodies. We have been afflicted by a poison we did not consume. I offer my heartfelt condolences to all those who lost their lives in this disaster and pray for the swift search of the missing and speedy recovery of the injured. I also make a strong demand to the government for the swift distribution of relief to the affected who are starving. On the 10th of Bhadra, 2083, not water but a huge mountain of dust, soil, and debris rose, shaking the ground and resembling an earthquake. That devastating landslide turned Rasuwa and many other districts into riverbanks, never to rise again, along with humans and all man-made structures in an instant.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Renu Chand.
Honourable Ms. Renu Chand (Nepali Communist Party): Honourable Chairperson, the government's Law Minister has lied. She is a liar. The National Assembly should clarify which bill it blocked and where it caused obstruction. How many bills has the government presented? How many have we blocked? How many have we returned? All this information should be provided. How dangerous is it for a minister to give false information to the public? She tried to defame the National Assembly, which is unacceptable. The Law Minister needs to answer. I urge the Chairperson to rule for an answer. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Vishnu Kumari Sapkota.
Honourable Ms. Vishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, I wish to pay heartfelt tribute on the occasion of the 113th birthday of the first elected Prime Minister, a towering figure, and a visionary leader, BP Koirala. Honourable Chairperson, there is a severe shortage of gas in the market. Even after standing in line for hours, citizens are unable to get gas and are forced to sit hungry. It is not a normal situation that despite having data on gas brought to Kathmandu via alternative routes after the road collapsed at Krishnabhir, the supply and distribution cannot be made smoothly. I wish to draw the government's attention through the Honourable Chairperson to immediately make the supply and distribution system transparent, control black marketing and artificial shortages, and arrange for gas to be easily available to citizens. I make a strong demand. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini.
Honourable Ms. Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, today the entire Nepali people are in a very sorrowful state. The devastating flood in Bhote Koshi has caused great loss of life and property. In such a dire situation, I urge the government through the Honourable House to prioritize rescue and relief with mind, word, and deed, setting aside all other matters, and to grant strength to the affected families for endurance. I pray to God that the missing people may return alive and urge the government to provide more resources to the local government for the swift provision of food, shelter, clothing, and medical treatment to the victims. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Vishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.
Honourable Mr. Vishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepali Communist Party): Honourable Chairperson, it has been 1 full year since the Janji rebellion and destruction. At that time, major cultural heritage sites were destroyed and looted. 76 people lost their lives, and a committee was formed under the leadership of Gauri Bahadur Khaki for investigation, and it submitted its report. The National Human Rights Commission also conducted an investigation and submitted a report, and both these reports are being hidden. The government is trying to shield the culprits by forming another committee. I wish to draw the government's attention to making both those hidden reports public and taking strict action against the culprits. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari.
Honourable Mr. Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepali Communist Party): Honourable Chairperson, the country is currently in national mourning following the deluge in the Bhote Koshi River. If the Nepali security rescue teams and experts had been mobilized on a war footing with modern rescue materials, equipment, and technology from the very beginning of the deluge, many of those trapped in the landslide could have been rescued alive. The government's attention has not been adequate towards the possibility of rescue in the geographically accessible areas like Nuwakot and Trishuli. The employees, workers, and laborers trapped in the tunnels of Trishuli 3A, Trishuli 3B, Chilime Hydropower, and Rasuwagadhi Hydropower are still hoping for their survival. I wish to draw the government's attention to intensifying excavation and search operations in the buried houses, debris, and public structures. I also make a strong demand to the government to coordinate with local levels for the scientific distribution of relief in remote areas for the management of corpses and distribution of relief.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the order of speaking during the Zero Hour concludes here. Honourable members, names have been received on a party basis to speak during the Special Time. I will now provide time for the Honourable members to speak. First, Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, time 9 minutes. Following this, Honourable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari.
Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, I am happy because 113 years ago today, a great human of Nepal, Bisheshwor Prasad Koirala, was born, whom we all know as BP Koirala. I bow down to the courage and the work he truly did in making the Nepali people citizens from subjects, and I offer my heartfelt tribute and respect to the venerable great human BP Koirala. I am also sad today because, exactly 1 year and 1 day ago, at this very time, we were living in extreme uncertainty, extreme fear, and extreme anxiety. We were struggling with a situation where we would look out of the window in distress, go to the roof in distress, and hide in rooms out of fear. I also offer my heartfelt tribute to all the martyrs and heroes of the nation who sacrificed their lives in the Janji movement, which was launched by the youth on Bhadra 23rd demanding good governance and an end to corruption.

Honorable Chairperson, the Gen Z movement of August 14, 2025 (2082 BS Bhadra 23) was not an incident that suddenly fell from the sky. It was an explosion of accumulated dissatisfaction within Nepali society for years. And after the government banned various social media platforms, the youth generation became agitated. But Chairperson, we must understand one thing: the ban on social media was not the only cause of the movement; it was merely the spark that ignited the explosion. The gunpowder had been accumulating within Nepali society for years. That gunpowder was corruption, that gunpowder was unemployment, that gunpowder was political favoritism, that gunpowder was nepotism and dynastic politics, that gunpowder was the pain of youth leaving the country due to lack of opportunities. Honorable Chairperson, we must learn a serious lesson here: when the voice of the people is not heard, movements are born; when movements are not heard, anger is born; and when anger is resolved incorrectly, the state itself can collapse. After that, we entered a serious political transition. An interim government was formed under the leadership of Sushila Karki, the House of Representatives was dissolved, and the country moved towards new elections. Honorable Chairperson, the Prime Ministership of Honorable Balen Shah is not just the success of one individual. It is a message from a generation, it is the expectation of the youth, it is dissatisfaction with the old political culture, and it is the voice of the people saying, we don't want to hear the same old speeches anymore; we want results now. But Chairperson, I want to clarify one thing here: new politics does not happen just because new faces appear. The system does not change just because a new person sits in an old chair. It is easy to change the government, but difficult to change the character of governance. Today, the public is looking with immense expectation at the government led by Honorable Prime Minister Balen Shah. The government talks about good governance, it talks about controlling corruption, it talks about digital and effective government services, it talks about administrative reform, it talks about providing opportunities to the new generation, it talks about an inclusive state, it talks about social justice, it talks about the rule of law. But Chairperson, the government will be evaluated not just by its manifesto but by its results. Today, the biggest problem in the country is still unemployment. Today, thousands of youth are still heading towards Tribhuvan Airport. Today, the fields in the villages are still barren; today, farmers are struggling to get a fair price for their produce; today, ordinary citizens still have to wait for hours to get services in government offices. Therefore, my question to the government is: the Prime Minister has changed, but has the future of Nepali citizens changed? The slogans have changed, but has the life of the citizens changed? I feel that the real success of the new government lies in the answers to these questions. And the government must work against corruption. Honorable Chairperson, corruption is one of the biggest demands of the people. But I want to tell the government clearly: action against corruption must be taken based on evidence, not on party affiliation. Even if a person is from the ruling party, if they are guilty, action must be taken; even if a person is from the opposition, if they are guilty, action must be taken. Whether from an old party or a new party, everyone must be equal in the eyes of the law. If the campaign against corruption is impartial, it will win the trust of the people. But if there is a tendency to protect some and catch only others, the public will see through it. Therefore, my clear request is: not revenge, but justice; not revenge, but justice is needed; not propaganda, but evidence is needed; not slogans, but results are needed. Honorable Chairperson, what was the biggest achievement of the Gen Z movement? In my opinion, that movement taught Nepali youth one thing: you are not just spectators; you are not just people who vote in elections; you are citizens who can question the state. But even after the movement, a challenge remains. The energy of the movement must be transformed into institutional change. The movement's goal is not fulfilled simply by changing the government. Because removing a Prime Minister might be a revolution, but reforming the system is real change. Today, we may be proud that we removed a government in the name of the Gen Z movement, but should we not ask whether the questions raised by that movement have been resolved? This is the biggest challenge standing before us. Honorable Chairperson, today I only want to tell the government from this house: do not make August 14th (Bhadra 23rd) a story of your political success; consider it a warning. Because the people can change governments, the people can change leaders, the people can change the direction of history. Citizens are seeking the right to live with dignity in their own country. Therefore, Nepali people now want new results, not new speeches. They want opportunities to build a future in Nepal, not policies that send youth abroad. They want effective and strong ministries, not popular ministers. They want ministers who can make laws for Dalits, not just any minister. Nepali citizens want gas in their homes, not assurances from ministers. Do they want air or a corpse? Honorable Chairperson, August 14th shook the power, but the question now is, have we been able to reform the state from it? If we fail to understand the pain of that movement, the anger of the youth, and the expectations of the people, we will have to keep searching for the reasons for the next movement. From this movement, we need not just a new Prime Minister, but a change in political culture and politics. Therefore, if we can advance our politics towards making August 14th not just a day of protest, but the beginning of a new Nepal, Nepal's prosperity will lie in that. I draw the attention of all political parties, the government, and everyone to this and end my speech here. Thank you, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari, (13:48 PM) Time 15 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dangal. Honorable Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepal Communist Party):- (13:49 PM) Honorable Chairperson, I stand at the rostrum of this esteemed assembly to draw special attention to the problems seen in rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and reconstruction in the affected areas due to the catastrophic flood in the Kairud river in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China on August 26th (Bhadra 10th), which caused loss of life and property in districts like Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, and Gorkha. I offer my deepest condolences to the deceased who lost their lives in the devastating flood of August 26th. I express deep sympathy to the families of the deceased. I wish for the speedy recovery of the injured. I urge the government to intensify the search for more than 5,000 missing domestic and foreign nationals. Honorable Chairperson, this catastrophe has erased the historical identity of Nuwakot and Rasuwa. It has erased the historical significance of the historic Betrawati Bazaar, the historic Trishuli Bazaar, and the historic Devighat. Among the most vulnerable affected by this disaster are lactating mothers, children, and the elderly. Nepal is currently in a state of national mourning and disaster. In the experience of floods and landslides over the last 100 years, we have faced such a terrible catastrophe for the first time in history. This destructive catastrophe has caused great loss of life and property. Its impact is not limited to Nuwakot, Rasuwa, Dhading, Gorkha, Chitwan, and Nawalparasi; dozens of districts in the country have been affected in one way or another. As of today, 1,366 bodies have been identified from more than three dozen districts. More than 4,000 people are missing. This disaster has not only affected Nepalis. More than 600 foreign nationals from 34 countries, including China and India, are missing. This figure is not limited to this. In terms of physical damage, according to data identified to date, 32,933 people from 7,470 households have been displaced. 48 government offices, 55 kilometers of road, 37 concrete bridges, 68 suspension bridges, and 1,806 hectares of arable land have been destroyed. Hydropower projects have been affected in production, with 783 megawatts of electricity from 13 hydropower projects. This is only the preliminary estimate of the damage. This damage is increasing day by day. Government data is changing daily. The damage caused by the Bhote Koshi catastrophe can only be overcome through the collective effort and commitment of all Nepalis and national unity. Coordination, cooperation, and national unity are necessary to strengthen the management of rescue, relief, temporary and permanent reconstruction work. To determine the clear responsibilities of the provincial government and local levels in relief, rescue, rehabilitation, and reconstruction work, and to create a joint mechanism for effective monitoring and accountability, and to maintain continuous coordination and cooperation with the representatives at the provincial level, I draw the attention of the government through the Honorable Chairperson to organize an all-party meeting and a National Coordination Council meeting, consult with all concerned parties, integrate the demands and sentiments of the parliament and local levels, build national strength, and create an environment to face this great disaster in a unified manner. Honorable Chairperson, the government probably did not imagine that it would have to face such a catastrophic disaster in history. Could the advance warning of landslides have been given earlier, with timely information? Where was the weakness in coordination? Its proper review is necessary, and serious improvements must be made in the information system in the coming days. The event has proven that our nation's resources, capacity, and strength alone are not sufficient for rescue operations of this scale of disaster. The government had to be vigilant from the beginning of the catastrophe. The Nepali Army and Armed Police Force had received special training for disaster response, but they lacked the modern equipment and technology required along with the training. If coordination could have been established with special rescue teams from India, China, South Korea, and Australia from the early days of the rescue, there would have been a possibility of rescuing all the engineers, staff, workers, and laborers trapped inside the tunnels of Rasuwagadhi Hydro, Chilime Hydro, Trishuli 3A, Trishuli 3B, and Laitad alive. The Nepali Army, Armed Police, and Nepal Police, as well as volunteers, who worked day and night risking their lives for rescue and relief of the injured without modern equipment and technology, have achieved whatever success they have achieved in rescue operations to date, and they deserve praise and much gratitude. I urge the government to intensify the systematic search and rescue operations by mobilizing necessary resources, technology, and equipment in coordination with the Nepali Army, Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, and people's representatives at all three levels of government, volunteers, and concerned families, keeping in mind that people may still be buried or trapped in houses, buildings, structures, hydropower projects, tunnels, powerhouses, and other locations. I request the government to create special relief packages, concessional loans, and necessary financial support for the revival of businesses, rehabilitation, and to assess the actual damage to industries, businesses, agriculture, and other economic activities in the flood-affected areas. Such catastrophes arising from the effects of climate change...

This could be just the prelude to the current catastrophe. Being aware of this, it is necessary to start working from the foundation of the current disaster to become self-reliant in skills, capabilities, and state-of-the-art equipment and experts needed for disaster response, not just disaster management. I would like to draw the government's serious attention to making arrangements so that in the coming days, we are not deprived of modern equipment and rescue teams with experts, including high-capacity drones, carrier-based equipment for mud removal, high-capacity search pumps, and flood rescue tools, which the government is currently requesting from the international community. Honorable Chairperson, although Nepal is not unaware of being among the countries prone to climate change and multiple disasters in the world, we are in high-risk of disasters. Our attention is less focused on awareness and vigilance. In Nepal, due to rising temperatures in the Himalayan region, melting glaciers, instability of glacial lakes and natural dams, excessive rainfall, flash floods, river erosion, landslides, and wildfires, there has been serious damage to human life, settlements, roads, bridges, and infrastructure. The increasing risk from hydropower projects and public infrastructure is no longer a distant future concern for us. According to natural disaster experts, many glacial lakes are at risk. Their water density is increasing. There is a risk of them bursting at any time and creating disasters again in all Himalayan rivers from east to west. Out of about 2,100 lakes, 72 are at that level. More than 80 percent of the population is at risk of floods, earthquakes, landslides, and extreme temperatures. We have already experienced more than 26 major glacial lake outburst flood events since 1970. The main cause of the current catastrophe is the impact of climate change, and we must pay attention to the fact that such catastrophes and super-catastrophes originating from climate change are looming in our near future. I would like to draw the government's attention to building a National Himalayan Reconstruction and Monitoring System by integrating earthquake measurement devices, satellite systems, automatic cameras, mobile apps, global river monitoring, water level measurement, weather stations, glacial lake monitoring drones, and satellite technology into a single system, and to arrange for immediate delivery of potential disaster information to communities in risk zones. The attention of the international community is currently focused on Nepal. Citizens from 35 countries have been affected by this disaster in some way. More than 30 countries are also extending a helping hand to Nepal for relief and rescue. To draw the attention of the international community to the increasing disaster risk in the Himalayan region due to global carbon emissions, temperature rise, and climate change, and to the catastrophic flood of the Bhote Koshi, and to mobilize international climate finance for climate justice, adaptation, and compensation, the Prime Minister must present a clear stance on behalf of Nepal at international forums including the United Nations General Assembly and call for cooperation from the world community. A National Himalayan Climate and Disaster Fund must be established to mitigate Himalayan disasters caused by climate change. The Government of Nepal must make effective diplomatic efforts with friendly countries and member states to mobilize green climate and adaptation funds, as well as other international climate finance, for investment in early warning, adaptation, and safe infrastructure development. Honorable Chairperson, the current super-disaster has devastated thousands of private homes, roads, bridges, administrative buildings, schools, health facilities, water supply and electricity structures, and religious and cultural structures, to the point of erasing their identity. The local economy has been severely damaged. According to preliminary international and government data, the number of damaged and uninhabitable houses is estimated to be up to 20,000. The damage to physical property and infrastructure is estimated to be billions of US dollars. In this situation, the objective of reconstruction cannot be merely to rebuild the destroyed structures in their original locations and forms. Nepal's reconstruction policy must be based on the principle of rebuilding safer, more scientific, modern, and climate-resilient settlements than before. It is necessary to identify suitable land for building safe settlements, planned resettlement of vulnerable settlements, construction of climate-resilient buildings and infrastructure, and management of river and stream corridors. An integrated national strategy is needed for the mitigation of glacial lake and glacial river risks, early warning systems, and mobilization of climate finance. Considering the current and future potential risks of disaster, it is necessary to prepare a national framework for reconstruction that is safe, scientific, and planned. Identify safe land for new settlement development and resettlement by scientifically evaluating geological and climate risks. Prepare modern and climate-resilient reconstruction standards for private housing, roads, bridges, administrative buildings, schools, health facilities, hydropower, and other public infrastructure. Prepare a safe land use and river corridor conservation policy in the risk-prone areas of the Bhote Koshi, Trishuli River, and other flood-affected areas across the country. Prepare a long-term security strategy against glacial lake outbursts, glacial melting, and other Himalayan climate-related risks. I would like to draw the government's attention to declaring areas along the riverbanks in currently flood-prone risk zones such as Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading as fully risk-prone by posting red stickers, prohibiting the construction of permanent physical structures and road networks in those locations, conducting geological studies, seismic risk studies, flood risk studies, landslide risk studies, testing soil bearing capacity, analyzing future climate scenarios, identifying suitable government land where drinking water can be made available, and posting green stickers for resettlement. Thank you, greetings. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal, 15 minutes, after this Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid. Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dahal (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- (2:04 PM) Honorable Chairperson, at this moment, we are in the difficult pain of the unimaginable human and physical damage caused by the catastrophic flood in the Bhote Koshi on August 10th. Exactly one year ago, the Nepali people experienced similar agonizing but different kinds of pain and destiny. On August 23rd last year, young people organized a peaceful protest demanding the restoration of good governance, an end to corruption, and the proper functioning of social media. Those demands were extremely just and were matters of common concern for all of us. I express my heartfelt tribute to the young people who lost their lives during the protest on August 23rd, wish for the recovery of the injured, and express deep sympathy to those who lost their loved ones. The then government had a policy of regulating social media, not banning it, and requiring registration according to the law. However, when the state failed to communicate that matter properly, young people accustomed to social media took to the streets. But the peaceful protest was hijacked, the movement was incited, children were forcibly brought to the street in school uniforms, security personnel were physically attacked, weapons were snatched, and the parliament building was violently attacked, and national and personal property was attacked, looted, and set on fire, leading to violent riots on August 24th. Government offices, private industries, and people's homes were burned, and massacres were carried out. In reality, this was a counter-revolution. It was a dangerous conspiracy to overthrow the state. Identifying the planners and protesters who set the country on fire and bringing them under the purview of legal action is the true respect for the spirit of the youth movement. For this, it is necessary to form an impartial investigation commission. It has become clear that the current government is not operating according to the spirit of the youth movement but according to the plans and sentiments of those who hijacked it. In such a situation, respecting the true spirit of the youth, ensuring good governance in the country, and establishing the rule of law are the needs of today. The CPN-UML is committed to respecting the spirit of the youth and addressing their just demands collaboratively. This party was in favor of the youth yesterday, is today, and will be tomorrow. I would like to inform you that we are committed to moving forward by correcting any shortcomings that may have occurred in the past regarding the spirit and demands of the youth. Honorable Chairperson, the first decision of the government formed after being elected in the last election was to arrest the former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and the then Home Minister. However, justice was served with the annulment of the arrest, which was extremely prejudiced, humiliating, and judicial, by the court. What is surprising in the events of August 23rd and 24th is, can a Nepali person do such a thing as burning the country? This is a serious question. Time will provide the answer. It is a serious matter of investigation that individuals who burned the country and broke jails yesterday have reached high positions in the state today. A drama was staged to form a so-called commission to investigate the loss of life and property in that incident and to produce a report according to their wishes. The report submitted by the person who distorted the conclusions of the movement is clearly biased and prepared with the intention of character assassination of the then leadership and institutionalizing politics of hatred. Regarding the report of the National Human Rights Commission in the context of that incident and its recommendations, something needs to be said. They also remained controversial. The report states that it does not clearly establish that the top officials of the then government gave any direct orders, but it recommends action against them. The report states that the incident was planned and prepared in advance. But it cannot clearly identify who the planners, decision-makers, and operators of that conspiracy were, and how they succeeded in reaching that stage, and bring them under the purview of action. The most serious and objectionable aspect of the report is the opinion expressed that action should be taken by enacting retroactive legal provisions. The Constitution of Nepal does not accept retroactive criminal law. The commission's constitutional duty is limited to the protection, investigation, and recommendation of human rights. Therefore, some of the commission's recommendations appear to have gone beyond constitutional limits, which is wrong and inappropriate. Honorable Chairperson, it is clear that the forces of domestic and foreign reactionaries were involved in the massacre of August 23rd and 24th. This anti-humanitarian massacre and treasonous act in the name of youth will be remembered by the Nepali people for ages as a dark day. Those who committed and facilitated this will be brought to justice sooner or later. In this process, democracy and the constitution, achieved through great sacrifice, were violated. I want to reiterate that the CPN-UML is determined to protect and develop democratic republic, federalism, secularism, inclusivity, and a socialist-oriented system. Honorable Chairperson, the person who played a role in inciting violence by agitating the situation in the field of protest was unconstitutionally handed over the leadership of the government. The head of the unconstitutional government

It was recommended to dissolve parliament unconstitutionally and it was dissolved. The person who directly led and directed that destruction was not with the democratic government or the President, but issued orders to the army. Today, it has become a tragedy that the country is being ruled by that undemocratic leadership. The movement of the youth has been hijacked by organizations like TOB, American Youth Council, Barbara Foundation, Hami Nepali, and their associates. Honorable Chairperson, why did KP Oli have to be removed as Prime Minister and his led government? There was a conspiracy with the government to prevent his government from being formed as much as possible, and if formed, to remove it from power as soon as possible. There are various reasons for this. 1. During the tenure of the previous government led by the then Communist Party of Nepal and KP Oli, 'Enough is enough, no not again' was chanted and the Singha Durbar was surrounded. The conspiracy to overthrow the government was happening at that time. 2. The government and its leadership were acting as guardians of nationality. 3. It protected the nation, nationality, national independence, national interest, territorial integrity, and national sovereignty. Earlier, in the process of constitution-making, it played a role in promulgating the constitution by rejecting the order issued by the King. 4. Immediately after the promulgation of the constitution, it firmly protested the anti-humanitarian blockade. 4. It led the effort to reclaim land encroached upon for a long time by establishing national consensus and including the encroached land in the new map in the constitution, and to reclaim the encroached land. 6. Role of Nepali Congress: The Nepali Congress mobilized party cadres from the first day of the disaster, the president himself visited the site, and deposited 1 crore rupees in the relief fund. Lack of scientific costing: The practice of distributing relief based on political affiliation should be ended, and digital and scientific verification should be started immediately. Build Back Better: Without repeating the old mistakes in geography, structures should be built to be disaster-resilient. Package: Special packages for agriculture and livelihood should be announced immediately, including concessional loans without collateral for those who lost their livelihoods, seeds, and employment. Psychosocial counseling: Psychiatrists should be immediately deployed in temporary camps for affected citizens suffering from severe mental trauma. Warning to abandon party interests: This is a national catastrophe. The government should abandon its inaction and create an integrated plan with the cooperation of all three levels of government and the opposition. Demand for a parliamentary inquiry committee: A high-level parliamentary committee should be formed to investigate the misuse of helicopters, the neglect of security and mechanisms, and the extreme negligence in rescue operations. I wish to draw the government's attention to these matters through the Honorable Chairperson. Thank you. Jai Nepal.

Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Chairperson of the Law Management Committee, Krishna Bahadur Rokaya, to present the committee's report to the assembly regarding the Bill to Revive the Previous Provisions of the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042, along with a message from the House of Representatives.

Honorable Chairperson of the Law Management Committee, Shri Krishna Bahadur Rokaya:-
(14:09 hrs)
Honorable Chairperson, the Bill to Revive the Previous Provisions of the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042, along with a message from the House of Representatives, was tabled in the National Assembly on Bhadra 27, 2083 BS. It was sent to the Law Management Committee for clause-by-clause discussion on Bhadra 9, 2083 BS, as per Rule 104 (1) (b) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Amendments were registered by 14 honorable members in three groups on two clauses of the bill, and these were approved by the Honorable Chairperson for discussion. The committee commenced discussions on the bill on Bhadra 15, 2083 BS. In the meeting, discussions were held with former secretaries of the Nepal Government, former heads of security agencies, and independent analysts as experts. On Bhadra 17, 2083 BS, the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sovita Gautam, clarified the objectives and reasons for presenting the bill on behalf of the Honorable Prime Minister Balen Shah, after which the honorable members who registered amendments presented their views regarding the amendments.

On Bhadra 18, 2083 BS, detailed clause-by-clause discussions were held on the bill in the committee meeting, in the presence of the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sovita Gautam, on behalf of the Honorable Prime Minister Balen Shah, along with the secretaries and joint secretaries of the Prime Minister's Office and the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. Previously, through the Act to Amend Some Nepal Laws, 2074, Section 4 (1) of the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042 was amended to place the Investigation Department, which was under the Ministry of Home Affairs, under the Prime Minister's Office. However, later, to facilitate coordination with security agencies under the Ministry of Home Affairs for information flow and analysis, the department was brought back under the Ministry of Home Affairs through an ordinance. In the context of the Nepal Government (Allocation of Business) Rules, 2083, having already amended the department to be under the Prime Minister's Office, the government presented this bill to the house to legally continue the provision of the National Investigation Department being under the Government of Nepal, Prime Minister's Office, by reviving the previous legal arrangement instead of the words 'Government of Nepal, Ministry of Home Affairs' as established by the ordinance.

During the committee's discussions on the bill, in the context of the country's geopolitical situation, the revolution in the information technology sector, diplomatic relations, residential embassies, countries with treaties and agreements, balanced diplomacy, and current security challenges, the need for internal and external espionage and intelligence agencies, counter-intelligence, and domestic intelligence was raised. It was also suggested to activate the National Security Council, as all security agencies have intelligence capabilities. Furthermore, the question was raised: How will the Home Minister be accountable if a part of the Ministry of Home Affairs is taken to another agency? In various countries, depending on their governance system, intelligence agencies are found under the President's Office, Prime Minister's Office, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or Ministry of Defense. This institution is a part of the government's legal construction priority list for this fiscal year, including the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042. Therefore, when the bill is presented to the house later, addressing these raised issues, the Bill to Revive the Previous Provisions of the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042, was unanimously passed in its preliminary form by the committee's meeting on Bhadra 18, 2083 BS. I wish to inform you of this.

Finally, I express my sincere gratitude to the Honorable Chairperson and the Honorable Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly for their guidance and coordination regarding this bill. I extend my heartfelt thanks to the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, the honorable members of the committee, and the honorable members who registered amendments for participating in the discussion of the bill in the committee. I also wish to thank the Secretary General of the Federal Parliament, the Secretary of the National Assembly, the secretaries of the secretariat, the secretaries and joint secretaries of the Prime Minister's Office and the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, former secretaries, former heads of security agencies, independent analysts who provided opinions and suggestions regarding the bill, and all the staff of the secretariat and journalists for facilitating the committee's work.

Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Honorable Chairperson, in accordance with Rule 114 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, I present to this esteemed assembly the report prepared by the committee after discussing the Bill to Revive the Previous Provisions of the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042. Thank you.
